output.title: When search becomes a workflow decision
output.body:
If you are rethinking search behaviour in a small business, start with one question: are people repeatedly searching your own business material, or the open web? That difference matters. Repeated searching through customer emails, past invoices, product specs, or help-desk notes is a workflow problem; random web research usually is not.

For a 1–10 person team, the practical check is simple: if that internal searching is taking a noticeable slice of the week and the result should be faster replies, fewer errors, or less back-and-forth, treat it as a bounded automation decision. Not a grand AI strategy. Just one repeatable task.

The control is document readiness. A knowledge assistant only makes sense when the useful material already exists in machine-readable form, such as MD, PDF, or structured data. Bareni has a self-built demo that retrieves from approved company documents rather than the open web. It works on synthetic data and runs locally; the public route is locked. OCR, scan ingestion, rate limiting, and billing are planned, not working.

Keep human approval in place if the search output affects customer communication or a business decision. The system can suggest; the owner decides. That is Bareni policy for high-risk decisions, not an absolute warranty.

One practical next step: map one recurring search task on paper, then check whether the source material is ready and whether you still want final review before anything goes out. If yes, the normal next step is a free 30-minute diagnostic to define the workflow, the pilot scope, and the measures, with no promise of a result.
